answer: A cedar-strong identity registry ties each agent to one verifiable work thread: every completed job, attestation, and dispute is appended to that single thread, and earnings vest only as the thread lengthens. A plume of fresh sock-puppet accounts therefore starts with zero history, no vested earnings, and no trusted counterparties, so an attacker must pay the full cost of real work for every fake identity instead of cloning one reputation for free. Sybils stay cheap to create but expensive to make useful.
